item.title: Argentina Fails in Bid to Halt UK Oil Activity Near Falklands
item.author: Alexander Weber
item.content:encoded: A United Nations-backed court rejected a request by Argentina seeking to halt a UK oil project near the Falkland Islands.

item.title: Millions of Children Are Losing Food Stamps
item.author: Jason DeParle and Emily Kask
item.content:encoded: Republicans said the cuts, part of their domestic policy bill, would root out fraud and push adults to work. But two million children have lost benefits.

item.title: This Seattle Engineering Marvel Hid a Mystery: Pyramids of Dead Fish
item.author: Anna Griffin
item.content:encoded: What could have caused the piles of carcasses beneath the mile-and-a-half-long floating bridge that extended Seattle’s light rail across a lake?

item.title: Australia’s Center-Right Coalition Routs Labor in Victoria
item.author: James Mayger
item.content:encoded: Australia’s Liberal-National coalition is set to win control of Victoria state, wiping out a deeply unpopular Labor government after 12 years of rule, national broadcaster ABC projected.

item.title: Burnham’s Europe Plan Still Taking Shape as Brexit Rivals Circle
item.author: Chloe Chaplain, Joe Mayes and Lucy White
item.content:encoded: Britain could not rejoin the European Union without another referendum, Prime Minister Andy Burnham said this week — much to the surprise of his own ministers and government officials.

item.title: Trump’s Embrace of Xi and Huang Stuns China Critics in Washington
item.author: Michael Crowley
item.content:encoded: Warnings from hard-liners have grown more urgent amid what some call a winner-take-all race for A.I. dominance.

item.title: What Happened to JFK-Era Intel Records?
item.content:encoded: Fifty years after John F. Kennedy's assassination, Disclosure podcast's Jason Leopold requested the US Defense Intelligence Agency's daily briefings for the surrounding two months, a potential trove of details about foreign governments' contemporary planning and reactions. Twelve years later, he received a response -- three days' worth of briefings, with redactions, 41 pages in all. Jason and co-host Matt Topic delve into the secrecy surrounding the Kennedy-era records, what has become of nearly two months' worth of briefings and what could have led to the destruction of intelligence reports from a pivotal moment in US history. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Supreme Court Rulings Cheered by Republicans Wound Up Hurting Them
item.author: Carl Hulse
item.content:encoded: Decisions on voting rights, immigration and corruption generated a backlash that helped spur turnout that drove the Democratic sweep of Congress.

item.title: Planning Board to Hold Last-Minute Meeting to Consider Trump’s D.C. Construction
item.author: Luke Broadwater
item.content:encoded: President Trump will lose control over the National Capital Planning Commission after Democrats take control of Congress in January. It could give final approval to some of his prized projects.

item.title: For One Stormy Moment, D.C. Reveled in a Blank Wall Where Trump’s Name Once Hung
item.author: Elizabeth Williamson
item.content:encoded: High winds dislodged a section of tarp obscuring the removal of the president’s name from the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts, whipping up some members of the capital.

item.title: Taiwan’s Ruling DPP Concedes Taipei Race, Gains Key Cities
item.author: Rebecca Choong Wilkins, Yian Lee and Chien-Hua Wan
item.content:encoded: Taiwan’s ruling Democratic Progressive Party conceded defeat in the race to win the Taipei mayoralty from the opposition Kuomintang’s Chiang Wan-an, even as it made significant gains elsewhere on the island in tightly fought local elections.

item.title: Five Big Questions for the 2028 Presidential Race
item.author: Tim Balk
item.content:encoded: Will JD Vance and Marco Rubio run? What about Kamala Harris and Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez? And, of course, what role will President Trump play?

item.title: Jailed Brazil Beach Soccer Star Drawn Into Russia-US Spy Dispute
item.author: Augusta Saraiva
item.content:encoded: A Brazilian beach soccer star has become an unlikely bargaining chip in a dispute over an alleged Russian spy who has been sought by both Moscow and Washington.

item.title: Sánchez Seeks Unlikely Win With Plea for Spaniards to Go Vote
item.author: Daniel Basteiro
item.content:encoded: Pedro Sánchez rallied voters to turn out in Sunday’s national election during his final campaign event, in a last-minute attempt to pull off an upset.

item.title: Meloni Seethes at Zelenskyy for Not Warning Her on Libya Strike
item.author: Donato Paolo Mancini and Daniele Lepido
item.content:encoded: Giorgia Meloni and Volodymyr Zelenskyy had a tense conversation over Ukraine’s failure to coordinate with its allies or give any advance warning about its strikes against Russian ships off Libya’s coast.

item.title: New York Senate Majority Leader Andrea Stewart-Cousins Dies
item.author: Raga Justin
item.content:encoded: New York Senate Majority Leader Andrea Stewart-Cousins died Friday, just weeks after being reelected to another term as head of one of the largest Democratic conferences in state history.

item.title: Lula Builds Brazil Cabinet With Alckmin, Banker Trabuco in Key Roles
item.author: Martha Beck and Augusta Saraiva
item.content:encoded: Brazil President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva is tilting toward the center as he builds the cabinet for his fourth and final term, tapping market-friendly officials to signal a more pragmatic economic approach while also placing trusted political allies in prominent roles as he mulls potential successors.

item.title: Old Foes Unite to Return Cosmetics Tycoon as Johannesburg Mayor
item.author: S'thembile Cele
item.content:encoded: Herman Mashaba won election as mayor of Johannesburg, returning to lead South Africa’s economic hub with the backing of the African National Congress — the party he helped oust from power in the city a decade ago.

item.title: France Joins the Dutch in Opposing Proposed US Export Curbs
item.author: Jorge Valero and Samy Adghirni
item.content:encoded: France said it’s backing the Dutch over concerns that a proposed US law will force European companies such as ASML Holding NV to comply with restrictions on technology exports to China, and is considering possible measures if the law is adopted.

item.title: In Democrats vs. Trump, the Loser May Be Federal Contractors
item.author: Luke Broadwater
item.content:encoded: The incoming Democratic majorities have begun targeting businesses and other outsiders in their planned inquiries, but the president has threatened to fire them if they comply without his permission.

item.title: Britain’s Richest Families Cushion Themselves From Rising Taxes and Costs
item.content:encoded:
Some of Britain’s richest families are taking steps to cushion themselves from higher taxes and wage costs.
Benjamin Stupples explains. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Nvidia Chips Turn Up at China Site Linked to Alice Huang
item.content:encoded: A pair of Chinese firms installed Nvidia Corp.’s powerful Blackwell semiconductors in a Shanghai data center linked to Alice Huang, the woman whose extramarital affair with CEO Jensen Huang is at the heart of a controversy surrounding the US chipmaker. Bloomberg's Tyler Kendall and Bloomberg Intelligence's Matt Bloxham have the details. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Le Pen’s Presidential Bid Hits Fresh Snag in Top Court Fight
item.author: Gaspard Sebag
item.content:encoded: Marine Le Pen’s previous vow to stand for the French presidency only if she can avoid being forced to wear an ankle monitor on the campaign trail has hit a potential snag.

item.title: Trump Turns the Tide to Score Early Wins in Defamation Suits
item.author: Erik Larson
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump’s poor track record in court in his defamation lawsuits against the press over the years is starting to turn around — at least for now.

item.title: Serbia’s New Leadership Picks Academic to Run for President
item.author: Misha Savic
item.content:encoded: Radomir Saicic, a tenured university professor who backed Serbia’s student-led movement that ousted longtime leader Aleksandar Vucic, will run for president in a popular vote next month.

item.title: Modi Government to Revive Plan to Expand India’s Parliament
item.author: Rajesh Roy
item.content:encoded: Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s administration is reviving an ambitious plan to expand the size of India’s parliament, people familiar with the matter said, after an earlier attempt was defeated when opposition parties joined forces against it.

item.title: Sweden’s Kristersson on Track to Clinch Second Term in Vote
item.author: Charlie Duxbury
item.content:encoded: Sweden’s Ulf Kristersson looks set to secure a second term as prime minister, even though he narrowly lost September’s election, after most lawmakers from a smaller party appeared ready to back him.

item.title: Bipartisan Desire to Regulate A.I. Faces Obstacles in Congress
item.author: Michael Gold and David McCabe
item.content:encoded: Members of both parties say they want to tackle artificial intelligence policy, but the slow pace of legislating and turf battles could stand in the way.

item.title: Thanksgiving Is Back on the Menu for Francesca Hong, the Failed Wisconsin Governor Candidate
item.author: Theodore Schleifer
item.content:encoded: Francesca Hong, who took heat over a social media post condemning the holiday during her run for the Democratic nomination, now has regrets — and is laughing it all off.

item.title: Argentina Senate Approves Bill to Suspend Primaries in Boost for Milei
item.author: Manuela Tobias and David Feliba
item.content:encoded: President Javier Milei won a trio of legislative victories, including support for the suspension of a primary vote before Argentina’s next election, that helped halt a slide in the country’s bonds.

item.title: How Our Reporters Navigate Politics at Thanksgiving
item.author: Megan DiTrolio, Michael Barbaro, Vanessa Friedman, Ruth Graham, Erica L. Green, Yair Rosenberg and Kim Severson
item.content:encoded: A holiday gathering can be joyous. And fraught. Here’s how six reporters deal with their own dinner-table discourse. (And when they switch the topic to serving spoons or animal sex.)

item.title: Strobe Talbott, Journalist Who Joined Clinton’s State Department, Has Died
item.author: Trip Gabriel
item.content:encoded: He was a reporter and foreign affairs columnist at Time and then served as deputy secretary of state and president of the Brookings Institution. He was 80.

item.title: Trump Administration’s Cuts to SNAP Threaten Free School Meals
item.author: Linda Qiu
item.content:encoded: The Trump administration’s cuts and proposed regulatory changes to the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program would have consequences for school lunch and breakfast.

item.title: How a Thanksgiving Tradition Connects to Presidential Powers
item.author: Peter Baker, Gilad Thaler, Brian Oh, Pierre Kattar and Shawn Paik
item.content:encoded: As President Trump pardons turkeys for Thanksgiving, our chief White House correspondent Peter Baker takes a look back at the history of the tradition and the presidential power of the pardon.

item.title: Border Barrier Cannot be Removed for Decades, Texas Republicans and D.O.J. Agree
item.author: Zach Montague
item.content:encoded: Just before Democrats take over the state government, Trump administration and outgoing Republican officials in Texas ink legal settlement barring removal of wire for 30 years.

item.title: Trump Rejoiced in the Market’s Nvidia Surge. It Didn’t Last Long.
item.author: David E. Sanger
item.content:encoded: The retreat of the stock market in recent days shows how President Trump’s push to reinstall the company’s chief executive has collided with the realities of his other policies.

item.title: Lukoil to Sell Foreign Assets, but Not to Kushner and Witkoff Associates
item.author: Eric Lipton and Anton Troianovski
item.content:encoded: Valuable properties belonging to the Russian energy giant will be sold to an American-led consortium. But Middle Eastern business contacts of the two Trump envoys pulled out because of political winds.

item.title: Sept. 11 Defendants Get New Opening to Challenge Death Penalty
item.author: Carol Rosenberg
item.content:encoded: At issue is a clause in a plea deal involving Khalid Shaikh Mohammed, the man accused of being the mastermind of the plot, and two other defendants.

item.title: C.I.A. Waterboarded More Detainees Than It Admitted, F.B.I. Interview Suggests
item.author: Charlie Savage
item.content:encoded: The apparent disclosure was included in files released in response to a New York Times lawsuit. The release also shed light on C.I.A. officials’ fears about possible prosecutions.

item.title: Van Hollen’s Challenge to Schumer Highlights Democratic Rift on Israel
item.author: Annie Karni
item.content:encoded: Senator Chris Van Hollen says his move to replace Senator Chuck Schumer as party leader isn’t about Israel, but his sharply critical stance toward the Jewish state has become a major fault line in the race.
